report:
Reviewed the entire checking_scope claim, all six implementation entries and all eleven associated tests. The requirements are whole selected-local-crate signature/body demand, reachable submodules/associated bodies/generated items regardless of visibility or selector presence, no eager dependency body checking, explicit failure/diagnostics for unsupported in-scope work, and no selector-driven demand narrowing.

observe::collect unconditionally calls check_crate before inspecting observation targets. check_crate/walk_module visits the local root, emits diagnostics for parse Error items and incomplete expansion, then walks every expanded direct symbol; local modules recurse. walk_symbol requests local function signatures and, if syntax has a body, body checking; it checks struct signatures/fields and enum signatures, visits trait/impl associated items through local_associated_items, and audits local use declarations even when unused. External symbol variants are explicit no-op branches for this traversal, so fixture checking does not recursively demand dependency bodies. Supported local body demand is independent of marker sets and visibility. Residual macro invocation, const/static/type alias work is explicitly rejected by unsupported diagnostics. Enum discriminants are preserved in CST and explicitly diagnosed as unsupported, rather than silently dropped. The parser rejects malformed/unsupported top-level or associated item syntax as Error; associated_items enumeration retains ownership and supplies function symbols to the same walk_symbol dispatcher.

The changed LocalUseSym::diagnostics now performs the generated-root ambiguity audit before its unresolved-import check. It is still reached from the unconditional Use branch, and its new resolver helper only affects emitted diagnostics, not traversal or selectors. Captured resolver and expansion helpers confirm this separation. Captured CompileTest::prepare always runs the host collect path and checks both compiler results before expectations; the independent rustc result cannot hide a Sage diagnostic mismatch. Captured function/enum query implementations confirm these calls perform semantic checking. Captured test setup explains the in-memory discriminant rendering fixture.

Test evidence: unselected_private_body_still_reports_errors checks the same private bad function produces one Sage diagnostic both with and without a marker on another function. modules_and_associated_bodies requires a completed type from a private associated body in a reachable separate module. macro_generated_errors_match_the_invocation asserts an error from a generated function body. signature_diagnostics_are_retained_once demands an invalid signature used by two bodies and expects one diagnostic. unused_import_is_checked verifies an otherwise unused bad use is audited. real_std accepts a std type without attempting to check external bodies (the exhaustive external no-op branches provide the direct structural evidence for that negative guarantee). malformed_body_is_not_silently_accepted and malformed_private_enum_signature_is_checked require Sage mismatch failures, the latter specifically unresolved type. enum_discriminant_body_is_not_silently_accepted independently accounts for rustc's error and still requires Sage's explicit unsupported diagnostic. valid_enum_discriminant_reports_sage_limitation snapshots that limitation when rustc accepts. enum_discriminants_survive_syntax_token_rendering asserts both retained discriminant nodes and exact rendered expressions, preventing the syntax erasure which would bypass rejection. No TODO/N/A entries are present; the unsupported-feature behavior is explicit diagnostic behavior permitted by the claim, not claimed full language support.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests --test review_semantics: 14 and 8 tests passed. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib unselected_private_body_still_reports_errors: 1 passed. These cover all eleven associated tests, with additional tests selected by the integration targets. No production changes were made. Source inspection and these assertions account for the complete demand-policy claim; no requested edits.
